items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $(M,g)$ be a compact smooth Riemannian manifold with smooth boundary, let $T>0$, and let $\Sigma=(0,T)\times\partial M$. Write $dS_g$ for the Riemannian volume density of the metric restricted to $T\partial M$, and give $\Sigma$ the product density $dt\,dS_g$. If a measurable function $f$ is locally integrable in every smooth product chart of $\Sigma$ and
$$\int_\Sigma f\psi\,dS_gdt=0\qquad\text{for every }\psi\in C_c^\infty(\Sigma),$$
then $f=0$ almost everywhere on $\Sigma$.

items.title: Smooth Whitney extension on compact sets

references.title: Hassler Whitney, Analytic Extensions of Differentiable Functions Defined in Closed Sets
references.locator: Theorem I (1934). The full smooth extension is derived below from the library's proved finite-order construction, not assumed from this citation.

items.statement:
Let $d,N\ge1$ and let $A\subset\mathbb R^d$ be compact. For every multi-index $\alpha$ prescribe a continuous function $f_\alpha:A\to\mathbb R^N$. Define $P_a^k(x)=\sum_{|\alpha|\le k}f_\alpha(a)(x-a)^\alpha/\alpha!$. Assume the full Whitney compatibility conditions: for every $k\ge0$ and $|\alpha|\le k$,
$$D^\alpha P_a^k(b)-f_\alpha(b)=o(|a-b|^{k-|\alpha|})\quad(a,b\in A,\ |a-b|\to0),$$
uniformly in $a,b$. Then a smooth $F:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^N$ exists with $D^\alpha F|_A=f_\alpha$ for all $\alpha$. The construction uses no choice axiom. For a compact parameter family of jets on the same $A$, all choices of scales can be made common, and the resulting extensions have uniformly bounded seminorms on compact sets, provided all coefficient bounds and all the Whitney remainder moduli are uniform in that family.

items.statement: Let $X$ be a smooth manifold with an auxiliary smooth Riemannian metric, let $J=[a,b]$ be a compact interval, and let $\beta:J\to X$ be a smooth embedding with nonzero derivative. The normal fiber at $s$ is $N_s\beta=\{v\in T_{\beta(s)}X:g(v,\dot\beta(s))=0\}$. A **formal scalar jet along $\beta$** means a family of symmetric coordinate Taylor coefficients $T_{i,\alpha}(s)$ on a finite coordinate cover of a tubular neighborhood, smooth in $s\in J$, whose formal Taylor series transform on overlaps by the ordinary chain rule for a scalar function. Then there is an open neighborhood $U$ of $\beta(J)$ and, for either scalar field $\mathbb K=\mathbb R$ or $\mathbb C$, an $F\in C^\infty(U;\mathbb K)$ whose transverse derivatives along $\beta$ realize every prescribed transverse coefficient $T_{i,\alpha}(s)$. The construction is uniform for a compact parameter family of such jets when all coefficient seminorms are uniformly bounded. The same assertion holds on a finite union $A$ of embedded compact segments provided the induced full ambient jets satisfy full Whitney compatibility on that compact union: in each coordinate chart, for every $k$ and $|\alpha|\le k$, the degree-$k$ Taylor polynomials $P_x^k$ satisfy $D^\alpha P_x^k(y)-D^\alpha P_y^k(y)=o(|x-y|^{k-|\alpha|})$ uniformly for $x,y\in A$ as $|x-y|\to0$. Tangential components of a full jet are obtained by differentiating the transverse coefficients along each segment and applying the coordinate chain rule. For parameter families on the same finite union, require these Whitney remainder moduli as well as all coefficient bounds to be uniform. The single-segment construction requires no choice axiom.

items.title: Simple Riemannian background

references.title: Mikko Salo, On geometric inverse problems and microlocal analysis, full author lecture notes
references.locator: §2.2, PDF pp. 7–9: strict convexity, nontrapping, and no-conjugate-points convention.

references.title: Gabriel P. Paternain, Mikko Salo, and Gunther Uhlmann, Geometric inverse problems, with emphasis on two dimensions
references.locator: Chapter 3, Definition 3.8.1 and Theorem 3.8.2, printed pp. 102–103: the standard compact connected simple-manifold convention.

items.statement:
Let $n\ge2$ and let $(M,g)$ be a compact, connected, nonempty smooth $n$-dimensional Riemannian manifold with smooth boundary. Let $\nu_{\mathrm{out}}$ be the outward unit normal and let $\nabla$ be the Levi–Civita connection of $g$. The boundary is **strictly convex** when
$$
g(\nabla_w\nu_{\mathrm{out}},w)>0
$$
for every boundary point and every nonzero boundary-tangent vector $w$. Use the curvature convention
$$
R(X,Y)Z=\nabla_X\nabla_YZ-\nabla_Y\nabla_XZ-\nabla_{[X,Y]}Z.
$$
A Jacobi field along a unit-speed geodesic $\gamma$ is a smooth vector field $J$ satisfying $D_t^2J+R(J,\dot\gamma)\dot\gamma=0$, where $D_tJ=\nabla_{\dot\gamma}J$. The manifold has **no conjugate points** if every positive-length unit-speed geodesic segment $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ has no nonzero Jacobi field with $J(a)=J(b)=0$. It is **nontrapping** if every maximal unit-speed geodesic starting in $M^\circ$ reaches $\partial M$ in finite forward and backward time. The pair $(M,g)$ is a **simple Riemannian background** if its boundary is strictly convex, it has no conjugate points, and it is nontrapping.

When $n=2$, this is the simple-surface convention used for the scalar geodesic X-ray transform on the required inverse-problems page.

items.title: Finite propagation for the wave equation on a Riemannian manifold

references.title: Medet Nursultanov and Lauri Oksanen, Introduction to inverse problems for hyperbolic PDEs (full lecture notes, arXiv:2311.06020v2)

items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $(M,g)$ be a compact, connected, nonempty smooth Riemannian manifold with nonempty smooth boundary, let $T>0$, and define the intrinsic distance $d_g(x,y)$ as the infimum of Riemannian lengths of piecewise $C^1$ curves in $M$ from $x$ to $y$. For a nonempty set $K\subseteq M$, write $d_g(x,K)=\inf_{y\in K}d_g(x,y)$; for nonempty sets $A,B\subseteq M$, write $d_g(A,B)=\inf_{a\in A,b\in B}d_g(a,b)$. Let $q\in C^\infty(M;\mathbb R)$ be independent of time; the solution functions may be real- or complex-valued. Set
$$L_q=\partial_t^2-\Delta_g+q(x),\qquad \Delta_g=\operatorname{div}_g\nabla_g.$$
For a smooth solution $u$ up to the boundary on $[0,T]\times M$, let $u_0=u(0,\cdot)$, $u_1=\partial_tu(0,\cdot)$, and let $h=u|_{[0,T]\times\partial M}$ be its Dirichlet boundary value. The support of a function is the closure of the set where it is nonzero.

(i) If $h=0$ and $\operatorname{supp}u_0\cup\operatorname{supp}u_1\subseteq K$ for a nonempty closed $K\subseteq M$, then
$$\operatorname{supp}u(t,\cdot)\subseteq\{x\in M:d_g(x,K)\le t\}\qquad(0\le t\le T).$$

(ii) If $u_0=u_1=0$ and $h(t,\cdot)=0$ for $0\le t\le s_0$ with $0\le s_0<T$, then
$$\operatorname{supp}u(t,\cdot)\subseteq\{x\in M:d_g(x,\partial M)\le t-s_0\}\qquad(s_0\le t\le T).$$
The same assertion holds backward in time for a smooth solution with zero terminal data and boundary value vanishing for $s_1\le t\le T$, with $0\le t\le s_1$ and $t-s_0$ replaced by $s_1-t$.

(iii) Let $q_1,q_2\in C^\infty(M;\mathbb R)$ be time independent, put $Q=\operatorname{supp}(q_1-q_2)$, and suppose $Q\ne\varnothing$ and $d_g(Q,\partial M)>T/2$. If $u$ solves $L_{q_1}u=0$ with zero initial data and smooth boundary value compactly supported in $(0,T)\times\partial M$, and $v$ solves $L_{q_2}v=0$ with zero terminal data and smooth boundary value compactly supported in $(0,T)\times\partial M$, then
$$\int_0^T\!\int_M(q_1-q_2)u(t,x)v(t,x)\,dV_g(x)\,dt=0.$$
This is the two-boundary-trip finite-time invisibility statement at the level of the interior pairing.

items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $(M,g)$ be a nonempty compact smooth Riemannian manifold of positive dimension with smooth boundary and $q$ a smooth real function. Set $H=L^2(M,dV_g)$, $V=H^1_0(M)$ and $c=1+\|q\|_\infty$. Then
$$b(u,v)=\int_M(\langle\nabla u,\nabla\bar v\rangle+(q+c)u\bar v)\,dV_g$$
is an equivalent Hilbert inner product on $V$. There are an $H$-orthonormal sequence $(e_j)$ complete in $H$ and positive numbers $\mu_j\to\infty$ such that $b(e_j,v)=\mu_j(e_j,v)_H$ for every $v\in V$, and
$$b(u,u)=\sum_j\mu_j|(u,e_j)_H|^2\qquad(u\in V).$$
For $A=-\Delta_g+q$, weak solutions $v\in V$ of $Av=f\in H^k(M)$ satisfy
$$\|v\|_{H^{k+2}(M)}\le C_k(\|f\|_{H^k(M)}+\|v\|_{L^2(M)}),\qquad k=0,1,\ldots.$$
Here integer Sobolev norms use any finite smooth atlas. For every nonnegative integer $a$, the inclusion $H^k(M)\to C^a(M)$ is bounded for all sufficiently large integers $k$.

items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $(M,g)$ be a compact, connected, nonempty smooth Riemannian manifold with nonempty smooth boundary, let $T>0$, and let $q\in C^\infty(M;\mathbb R)$ be independent of time. Let $dV_g$ be Riemannian volume, let $\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$ be the scalar field, and set $L^2(M)=L^2(M,dV_g;\mathbb K)$. For complex scalars, the $L^2$ inner product is $(u,v)_{L^2}=\int_M u\overline v\,dV_g$, linear in its first argument; extend $g$ complex-bilinearly and set $|\nabla_gu|_g^2=\langle\nabla_gu,\nabla_g\overline u\rangle_g$. A weak coordinate derivative $D_iw$ is defined by $\int w\,\partial_i\psi=-\int D_iw\,\psi$ for every smooth compactly supported coordinate test $\psi$. Let $H^1(M;\mathbb K)$ be the space of $L^2(M;\mathbb K)$ functions whose weak coordinate first derivatives are locally $L^2$ in smooth charts and whose weak differential has finite metric $L^2$ norm; write $\nabla_gu$ for the metric dual of that weak differential. Give it norm
$$\|w\|_{H^1(M;\mathbb K)}^2=\int_M(|w|^2+|\nabla_gw|_g^2)\,dV_g,$$
and let $H_0^1(M;\mathbb K)$ be the closure of $C_c^\infty(M^\circ)$ in this norm. For $u_0\in H_0^1(M;\mathbb K)$, $u_1\in L^2(M;\mathbb K)$, and $F\in L^1((0,T);L^2(M;\mathbb K))$, there is a unique energy solution of the homogeneous Dirichlet problem
$$u_{tt}-\Delta_gu+q(x)u=F,\qquad u|_{(0,T)\times\partial M}=0,\qquad (u(0),u_t(0))=(u_0,u_1),$$
where energy solution means
$$u\in C([0,T];H_0^1(M;\mathbb K))\cap C^1([0,T];L^2(M;\mathbb K)),$$
and, for every $\phi\in H_0^1(M;\mathbb K)$ and every real-valued $\zeta\in C_c^\infty(0,T)$, the weak equation is
$$\int_0^T(u(t),\phi)_{L^2}\zeta''(t)\,dt+\int_0^T\!\int_M\big(\langle\nabla_gu(t),\nabla_g\overline{\phi}\rangle_g+q\,u(t)\overline{\phi}\big)\zeta(t)\,dV_gdt=\int_0^T(F(t),\phi)_{L^2}\zeta(t)\,dt.$$
There is a constant $C=C(M,g,q,T)<\infty$ such that
$$\sup_{0\le t\le T}\big(\|u(t)\|_{H^1(M;\mathbb K)}+\|u_t(t)\|_{L^2(M;\mathbb K)}\big)\le C\big(\|u_0\|_{H^1(M;\mathbb K)}+\|u_1\|_{L^2(M;\mathbb K)}+\|F\|_{L^1((0,T);L^2(M;\mathbb K))}\big).$$
In particular, the solution $w$ with zero initial data satisfies the correction estimate
$$\sup_{0\le t\le T}\big(\|w(t)\|_{H^1(M;\mathbb K)}+\|w_t(t)\|_{L^2(M;\mathbb K)}\big)\le C\|F\|_{L^1((0,T);L^2(M;\mathbb K))}.$$
The corresponding assertion for prescribed terminal data follows by time reversal. For smooth Dirichlet data compactly supported away from the time endpoints, the boundary lifting in the Riemannian Green-and-lifting lemma reduces the problem to this homogeneous-boundary assertion.

items.title: Time-dependent Dirichlet-to-Neumann map for the wave equation

references.title: Mikko Salo, On geometric inverse problems and microlocal analysis (full author lecture notes, arXiv:2312.08123v1)
references.locator: §3.1, forward map and full time-dependent boundary map conventions, PDF pp. 22–24; the local definition states the classical trace class needed for the boundary pairing.

items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $(M,g)$ be a compact, connected, nonempty smooth Riemannian manifold with smooth boundary, let $T>0$, and write $Q=(0,T)\times M$ and $\Sigma=(0,T)\times\partial M$. Let $q\in C^\infty(M;\mathbb R)$ be independent of time, and let $L_q=\partial_t^2-\Delta_g+q$. Write $\mathcal H=C_c^\infty(\Sigma)$ for smooth Dirichlet data compactly supported away from the temporal endpoints. Assume that for every $h\in\mathcal H$ the zero-initial-data Dirichlet problem $L_qu=0$, $u|_\Sigma=h$, $(u(0),u_t(0))=(0,0)$ has a unique solution $u_{q,h}\in C^2([0,T]\times M)$. Define the full time-dependent Dirichlet-to-Neumann map by
$$\Lambda_q^+ :\mathcal H\to L^2(\Sigma,dS_gdt),\qquad \Lambda_q^+h=\partial_{\nu_{out}}u_{q,h}|_\Sigma,$$
where $\nu_{out}$ is the outward unit normal. Also assume that for every $k\in\mathcal H$ the terminal-data Dirichlet problem $L_qv=0$, $v|_\Sigma=k$, $(v(T),v_t(T))=(0,0)$ has a unique solution $v_{q,k}\in C^2([0,T]\times M)$, and define
$$\Lambda_q^- :\mathcal H\to L^2(\Sigma,dS_gdt),\qquad \Lambda_q^-k=\partial_{\nu_{out}}v_{q,k}|_\Sigma.$$
The Green boundary pairing is the bilinear pairing $\int_\Sigma h\,\partial_{\nu_{out}}v\,dS_gdt$; the classical normal trace is in $L^2(\Sigma)$ for each stated $C^2$ solution class. Equality of two forward maps means equality on every $h\in\mathcal H$ over the whole time interval $(0,T)$, with the analogous convention for terminal maps.

items.title: Gaussian beams concentrated on an embedded null bicharacteristic
items.proof_strategy: complex phase, Riccati transport, Borel summation, and energy correction

references.title: Lauri Oksanen, Mikko Salo, Plamen Stefanov, and Gunther Uhlmann, Inverse problems for real principal type operators (arXiv:2001.07599v2)
references.locator: §3, Theorem 3.1, PDF p. 21 and proof through PDF p. 33: endpoint-localized residual, transported mass, phase, Riccati positivity, transport, Borel realization and patching. The no-cusp local phase argument is supplied below.

references.title: Mikko Salo, On geometric inverse problems and microlocal analysis (full author lecture notes, arXiv:2312.08123v1)
references.locator: §3.4, PDF pp. 32–39: Gaussian-beam construction sketch and its explicit proof boundary.

items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $X$ be a smooth spacetime manifold of dimension $m\ge2$ with a smooth positive density, and let $P=\sum_{|\alpha|\le2}a_\alpha(x)D^\alpha$ be a scalar second-order differential operator with smooth coefficients in local coordinates. In each local chart, use the microlocal convention $D_j:=(1/i)\partial_{x_j}=-i\partial_{x_j}$ and $D^\alpha:=D_1^{\alpha_1}\cdots D_m^{\alpha_m}$. Its principal symbol $p(x,\xi)=\sum_{|\alpha|=2}a_\alpha(x)\xi^\alpha$ is real and satisfies $dp\ne0$ on $\{p=0\}\subset T^*X\setminus0$. Equip $T^*X$ with its canonical cotangent symplectic form and define the Hamilton vector field by $\iota_{H_p}\omega_{\rm can}=dp$. A null bicharacteristic is a nonzero integral curve of $H_p$ contained in $\{p=0\}$. Let $\Gamma$ be a compact phase-space segment that is an injective immersion with no repeated phase points; assume its base projection is an immersion (the no-cusp condition) and that the segment is contained in the interior of $T^*X\setminus0$. For every integer $N\ge1$, there are complex smooth functions $u_\lambda$ formed from finitely many branch-local packets, each supported in a fixed tubular neighborhood of an embedded local branch of the base projection of $\Gamma$. Their longitudinal cutoffs equal one on the portion under observation and are supported in the chosen branch extensions. As $\lambda\to+\infty$, they have the following properties:

1. On each embedded local branch of the base projection, the phase has a formal transverse Taylor expansion solving the complex eikonal equation to every prescribed finite order; its transverse imaginary Hessian is positive definite and yields Gaussian decay away from that branch. At projected crossings the beam is the finite sum of the branch-local packets; a single phase on the crossing union is not required.
2. On each branch the amplitudes solve the transport hierarchy to the corresponding order and are realized by a Borel sum; the finitely many branch-local packets are patched and summed using their compatible jets.
3. Write $s$ for a fixed smooth parameter on the projected curve and fix its origin. There is a smooth positive transported density $w(s)ds$, normalized by $w(0)=1$, such that the measures $|u_\lambda|^2dV_X$ converge against compactly supported smooth tests away from endpoint neighborhoods to $\int a(\pi\Gamma(s))w(s)ds$. The weight is the one determined by the leading transport equation; a general operator with complex lower-order coefficients need not give constant $w$. For the real formally self-adjoint wave operator, with parameter equal to physical time along a unit-speed spatial ray and the wave phase normalized by $|\partial_t\phi|=1$, the transport gives $w=1$.
4. For every compact set $K$ disjoint from neighborhoods of the two projected endpoints, $\|Pu_\lambda\|_{L^2(K)}=O(\lambda^{-N})$ for each requested $N$, after carrying the expansions sufficiently far. The endpoint cutoff generally produces a residual near those endpoints. In particular, if the segment extends outside a compact measurement domain and its two endpoint neighborhoods are disjoint from that domain, the residual has the asserted order throughout that domain.

The cutoff in the ambient extension is one along the portion of the ray under observation and vanishes beyond the extended endpoints. A segment wholly in the spacetime interior does not have a globally negligible endpoint residual. Its tube can be supported away from the boundary and then has zero boundary trace; a wave beam entering and exiting a measurement domain instead has its actual smooth boundary trace there. For the energy-correction specialization, let $Q=(0,T)\times M$ with $T>0$, where $(M,g)$ is compact, connected, nonempty and smooth with nonempty smooth boundary, use density $dt\,dV_g$, and assume $P|_Q=\partial_t^2-\Delta_g+q(x)$ with $q\in C^\infty(M;\mathbb R)$ independent of time. If the two endpoint cutoff neighborhoods are disjoint from $Q$ and the extended beam is zero near the required initial or terminal time, the zero-boundary energy correction on this cylinder gives an exact solution with the same boundary data and an $O(\lambda^{-N})$ energy error for any requested $N$. The claim concerns an embedded segment in phase space and permits projected self-intersections.

items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $(M,g)$ be a compact, connected, nonempty simple Riemannian background of dimension $n\ge2$ with smooth strictly convex boundary, no conjugate points, and nontrapping geodesics. Fix $x_0\in\partial M$. For an inward unit vector $\omega\in T_{x_0}M$ with $g(\omega,
u_{out})<0$, let $\gamma_{x_0,\omega}$ be the unit-speed geodesic starting at $(x_0,\omega)$, and let $	au(x_0,\omega)>0$ be its first positive boundary-exit time. Define
$$\mathcal D_{x_0}=\{s\omega: g(\omega,\omega)=1,\ g(\omega,
u_{out})<0,\ 0<s<	au(x_0,\omega)\}\subset T_{x_0}M,$$
and define $E_{x_0}:\mathcal D_{x_0}	o M^\circ$ by $E_{x_0}(s\omega)=\gamma_{x_0,\omega}(s)$. Then $E_{x_0}$ is a diffeomorphism. In particular every interior point is joined to $x_0$ by a unique minimizing geodesic, the function $r_{x_0}(y)=d_g(x_0,y)$ is smooth on $M^\circ$, and on each ray tube it satisfies $|
abla_g r_{x_0}|_g=1$. The no-return extension of $M$ across its boundary is complete, and each outward or tangent geodesic launched from the boundary leaves $M$ permanently.

items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $(M,g)$ be a compact, connected, nonempty smooth Riemannian manifold with smooth boundary, let $T>0$, and let $q_1,q_2\in C^\infty(M;\mathbb R)$ be independent of time. Write $Q=(0,T)\times M$, $\Sigma=(0,T)\times\partial M$, and $P=\partial_t^2-\Delta_g$. For $h,k\in C_c^\infty(\Sigma)$, let $u$ be the zero-initial-data solution for $P+q_1$ with boundary value $h$, and let $v$ be the zero-terminal-data solution for $P+q_2$ with boundary value $k$, in the classical solution classes used to define the forward map $\Lambda_{q_1}^+$ and terminal map $\Lambda_{q_2}^-$; thus $u,v\in C^2([0,T]\times M)$. Then
$$\int_0^T\!\int_M(q_1-q_2)u(t,x)v(t,x)\,dV_g(x)\,dt=\int_0^T\!\int_{\partial M}\big(k\,\Lambda_{q_1}^+h-h\,\Lambda_{q_2}^-k\big)\,dS_g\,dt.$$
The boundary factors are paired bilinearly, without complex conjugation, and each normal derivative is the outward classical normal trace.

items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $(M,g)$ be a compact, connected, nonempty simple Riemannian background of dimension $n\ge2$, let $T>0$, and let $q_1,q_2\in C_c^\infty(M^\circ;\mathbb R)$ be static potentials. Let $\gamma:[0,L]\to M$ be a maximal unit-speed geodesic with $0<L<T$, and choose a time shift $t_0$ with $0<t_0<T-L$. In a nonsingular geodesic-polar tube about $\gamma$, there are conjugate eikonal phases and transport amplitudes, with a transverse cutoff of width $\varepsilon_\lambda=\lambda^{-1/(n+8)}$, that produce approximate forward and terminal solutions for the two wave operators. After solving the transport hierarchy through the required finite order and correcting the residual by the zero-data energy solver, the exact solutions have remainders $R_{j,\lambda}$ satisfying
$$\|R_{j,\lambda}\|_{L^\infty(0,T;H^1(M))}\le C\lambda^{-1}\|\chi_\lambda\|_{W^{4,\infty}},\qquad \|R_{j,\lambda}\|_{L^2((0,T)\times M)}=O(\lambda^{-1/2}),$$
where $\chi_\lambda$ is the stated transverse cutoff and $C$ is independent of $\lambda$. The normalized product of the forward and terminal exact solutions converges against every compactly supported smooth spacetime test function to integration along the null ray $(t_0+s,\gamma(s))$, $0\le s\le L$, with the Gaussian normalization fixed so that the limiting transverse integral is one.

items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $(M,g)$ be a compact, connected, nonempty simple Riemannian background of dimension $n\ge2$, with smooth boundary, let $T>0$, and let $q_1,q_2\in C_c^\infty(M^\circ;\mathbb R)$ be static interior potentials. Suppose the full time-dependent forward Dirichlet-to-Neumann maps for $\partial_t^2-\Delta_g+q_1$ and $\partial_t^2-\Delta_g+q_2$ agree for every smooth Dirichlet input compactly supported in $(0,T)\times\partial M$. Let $\gamma:[0,L]\to M$ be any unit-speed geodesic segment with $\gamma(0),\gamma(L)\in\partial M$, $\gamma((0,L))\subset M^\circ$, directed inward at $0$ and outward at $L$, and with length $0<L<T$. Then
$$\int_0^L(q_1-q_2)(\gamma(s))\,ds=0.$$

items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. Let $(M,g)$ be a compact, connected, nonempty simple two-dimensional Riemannian background with smooth boundary. Suppose $L_*<\infty$ bounds the lengths of all maximal unit-speed geodesics in $M$, and let $T>L_*$. For real static potentials $q_1,q_2\in C_c^\infty(M^\circ;\mathbb R)$, if the full time-dependent Dirichlet-to-Neumann maps for $\partial_t^2-\Delta_g+q_1$ and $\partial_t^2-\Delta_g+q_2$ agree for every smooth boundary input compactly supported in $(0,T)\times\partial M$, then $q_1=q_2$ on $M$. This equality statement asserts no stability modulus or recovery in the presence of noisy data.

items.statement:
Let $(M,g)$ be a compact Riemannian manifold, let $T>0$, and let $Q=(0,T)\times M$ carry product measure $dV_gdt$. Fix a unit-speed geodesic segment $\gamma:[0,L]\to M$ and $t_0$ with $0<t_0<T-L$, and set $\Gamma(s)=(t_0+s,\gamma(s))$, $0\le s\le L$; $ds$ denotes its arclength parameter. Let $a\in C^\infty([0,T]\times M)$, and for each $\lambda\ge1$ let $u_{j,\lambda}^{\mathrm{app}}\in L^2(Q)$ and $R_{j,\lambda}\in L^2(Q)$ for $j=1,2$. Suppose $\|u_{j,\lambda}^{\mathrm{app}}\|_{L^2(Q)}\le C_0$, $\|R_{j,\lambda}\|_{L^2(Q)}\le C_1\lambda^{-1/2}$, and
$$\int_Q a\,u_{1,\lambda}^{\mathrm{app}}u_{2,\lambda}^{\mathrm{app}}\,dV_gdt\longrightarrow \int_0^L a(t_0+s,\gamma(s))\,ds.$$
Set $u_{j,\lambda}=u_{j,\lambda}^{\mathrm{app}}+R_{j,\lambda}$. Then
$$\left|\int_Q a\,u_{1,\lambda}u_{2,\lambda}\,dV_gdt-\int_Q a\,u_{1,\lambda}^{\mathrm{app}}u_{2,\lambda}^{\mathrm{app}}\,dV_gdt\right|=O(\lambda^{-1/2}),$$
and hence the exact-solution product has the same ray-integral limit. For the real self-adjoint wave application, assume additionally Countable Choice, that $M$ is connected and nonempty with nonempty smooth boundary, and that the two operators are $P_j=\partial_t^2-\Delta_g+q_j(x)$ with $q_j\in C^\infty(M;\mathbb R)$ independent of time. The beams must satisfy the following additional supplier conditions: the observed ray has a compact embedded phase-space extension with immersed base projection; its two endpoint cutoff neighborhoods lie outside the measurement cylinder; and the approximate forward beam vanishes near $t=0$, while the approximate terminal beam vanishes near $t=T$. These temporal vanishing conditions are separate from the location of the spatial endpoint residuals. Use physical time along the unit-speed spatial ray and the normalization $|\partial_t\phi|=1$, with initial transported mass one. Then the Gaussian-beam lemma gives the unweighted ray measure and residual $O(\lambda^{-N})$ throughout $Q$. Apply the wave energy wellposedness theorem with zero boundary data and zero initial data for the forward correction, or zero terminal data for the terminal correction, to the negative residual. Since $\|P_ju_{j,\lambda}^{\mathrm{app}}\|_{L^1_tL^2_x}\le\sqrt T\|P_ju_{j,\lambda}^{\mathrm{app}}\|_{L^2(Q)}$, its energy estimate gives an $L^2(Q)$ correction $O(\lambda^{-N})$, hence the assumed $O(\lambda^{-1/2})$ order after choosing $N\ge1$. The exact waves retain the actual approximate boundary traces. This application asserts no temporal vanishing merely from an extension outside the measurement domain; the generic error estimate above only needs its explicitly stated norm and product-limit hypotheses.

items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $(M,g)$ be a compact, connected, nonempty smooth Riemannian manifold with nonempty smooth boundary, let $T>0$, and let $q_1,q_2\in C^\infty(M;\mathbb R)$ be time independent. Put $Q_0=\operatorname{supp}(q_1-q_2)$, the closure of the set on which $q_1-q_2$ is nonzero, and suppose $Q_0\ne\varnothing$ and $d_g(Q_0,\partial M)>T/2$, where $d_g$ is the intrinsic Riemannian distance. For every smooth Dirichlet input $h\in C_c^\infty((0,T)\times\partial M)$, the full time-dependent forward Dirichlet-to-Neumann maps satisfy
$$\Lambda_{q_1}^+h=\Lambda_{q_2}^+h\quad\text{in }L^2((0,T)\times\partial M,dS_gdt).$$
Thus a perturbation supported farther than half the observation time from the boundary cannot be detected by boundary measurements made before time $T$.

items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $(M,g)$ be a compact, connected, nonempty simple two-dimensional Riemannian manifold with smooth boundary. Suppose $L_*<\infty$ is an upper bound for the lengths of all maximal unit-speed geodesics in $M$. Let $T>L_*$ and let $q_1,q_2\in C_c^\infty(M^\circ;\mathbb R)$ be static interior potentials. If their full time-dependent Dirichlet-to-Neumann maps agree for every smooth boundary input compactly supported in $(0,T)\times\partial M$, then $q_1=q_2$ throughout $M$.

This gives a concrete observation-time condition: observing longer than a uniform upper bound on the maximal geodesic lengths suffices for coefficient uniqueness in the simple-surface case.
